text:
tess_prod_owner: Hey team — after we turned up the new Direct Connect VIF to customer-peering this morning, our Private prod in us-west-2 started throwing 502s to the Redwood control plane and internal service discovery is failing. This started at ~08:03PT. Can someone triage?

maria_support: Sorry you're hitting this, can you post traceroutes/dig output for the failing host and a short summary of the peering change you made?

tess_prod_owner: Sure. We added a second VIF to offload traffic to the customer's router, they enabled route-reflection on their edge. We also modified split-horizon DNS so the customer path should return private IPs over DX. Below is a tcpdump from one of the private nodes showing SYN -> no ACK to control plane.

```
08:09:12.345678 IP 10.10.2.14.54332 > 172.18.5.21.443: Flags [S], seq 123456789, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
08:09:12.345890 IP 10.10.2.14 > 172.18.5.21: ICMP 10.10.2.14 udp port 12345 unreachable, length 36
```

(tl;dr: TCP syn never completes, and internal hostname resolution returns public IPs intermittently)

jordan_sre: @tess_prod_owner can you run `dig +short @10.10.1.10 internal-svc.prod.local` and `traceroute -n 172.18.5.21` from the same node and paste results? Also what BGP ASN/advertised prefixes did the customer start advertising?

tess_prod_owner: dig: 

```
10.10.2.14
```

traceroute: 

```
traceroute to 172.18.5.21 (172.18.5.21), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.10.2.1  0.7 ms  0.6 ms  0.6 ms
 2  169.254.1.1  1.2 ms  1.3 ms  1.2 ms
 3  10.254.0.2  2.1 ms  2.0 ms  2.0 ms
 4  172.18.5.21  3.3 ms  3.3 ms  3.2 ms
```

(note: traceroute reaches control plane IP but TCP handshake fails)

alan_netops: The ICMP port unreachable is interesting — looks like an MTU/encapsulation mismatch or intermediary firewall dropping TCP. Did they change any route-maps or next-hop rewrite? Also what routes do we see on the Direct Connect BGP session?

devon_oncall: I pulled the BGP table from the DX router (customer-facing): 

```
BGP table: AS65051 via 192.0.2.2 - announced: 10.10.0.0/16, 172.18.0.0/24
Route-reflector is ON at the customer edge, ADVERTISE more specifics: 10.10.2.0/24
```

maria_support: Two immediate hypotheses: 1) split-horizon DNS now returning different (private) answers depending on which VIF you hit and some requests are going out the wrong path (asymmetric routing) causing reply packets to be dropped; 2) their edge is rewriting next-hops or doing proxy-ARP causing traffic to hit a firewall that blocks high-port ephemeral TCP.

jordan_sre: Can we confirm the control plane IP (172.18.5.21) is reachable from both VIFs and that return path uses the same ASN/next-hop? From our side, control plane expects src IPs from 10.10.0.0/16 and we have an allowlist for that range. If customer is SNATing traffic to a different IP, that could explain the 502s.

tess_prod_owner: Good point — we saw logs showing some requests hitting control plane with src 198.51.100.45 (public). The split-horizon should not be returning public addresses to private nodes. We suspect route-reflection caused them to prefer a path that goes out to the internet edge.

alan_netops: Can you run `tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 172.18.5.21` while initiating a curl and capture both outgoing SYN and incoming packets? We need to see src/dst on the reply. Also check `show ip bgp 10.10.2.0/24` on the DX router to see next-hop.

tess_prod_owner: Captured output attached below (excerpt):

```
10:12:05.123456 IP 10.10.2.14.54332 > 172.18.5.21.443: Flags [S]
10:12:05.123789 IP 172.18.5.21.443 > 198.51.100.45.54332: Flags [R]
```

maria_support: That RST goes to 198.51.100.45 — so replies are getting SNATed/translated to a public source before returning. This will break TCP from the private node because the node's syn expects reply to 10.10.2.14. Where is the SNAT happening? Customer edge? Transit?

jordan_sre: On our control plane, we don't SNAT to 198.51.100.45. Looks like the customer's edge is performing NAT for flows leaving their network to the control plane. Ask them to disable SNAT for the prefixes advertised over the DX VIF, or create a policy to preserve source. Also check their firewall for 'established' vs 'related' behavior.

alan_netops: Another angle: route-reflector could be reflecting a less specific 0.0.0.0/0 or public route into the private VRF by mistake. Customer should verify route-targets and ensure VRFs separate public/infrastructure routes. If the private VRF receives default route via route-reflector, egress will go out internet and SNAT will occur.

devon_oncall: Repro steps we used: 1) from private node: curl -v https://172.18.5.21/health -> SYN sent, no TLS handshake, 2) tcpdump showed RST to public IP 198.51.100.45, 3) BGP from DX shows 10.10.0.0/16 present but default route also visible in private VRF.

maria_support: Short-term mitigation: ask customer's network team to withdraw the default from the private VRF or add a static route for control-plane subnet pointing to the correct next-hop. Also add a firewall rule to avoid SNAT for 10.10.0.0/16 -> 172.18.5.0/24.

jordan_sre: We'll also adjust our ingress policy to accept requests from 198.51.100.45 temporarily and mark this as a degraded state. But it's better they fix NAT/VRF boundaries. I'll open a P1 ticket with infra to let the ops team know.

tess_prod_owner: I've pinged customer NOC and they confirmed they enabled route-reflection and a misapplied route-map pushed default into the private VRF. They're reverting now. They also said they added an SNAT policy for monitoring — removing that as well.

deploy-bot: Incident created: INC-2027-4082 assigned to netops oncall; priority: P1; link: https://redwood.incidents/INC-2027-4082

maria_support: Thanks. After their revert we should run a full regression: 1) verify dig returns private IPs only, 2) confirm tcp handshake completes, 3) check logs for 502s over the next hour. Can someone own verification?

jordan_sre: I'll run checks. Note for postmortem: add a playbook step to validate VRF default routes after any new VIF or route-reflector config. Also include a DNS split-horizon verification checklist.

tess_prod_owner: Confirmed at 09:02PT the customer reverted change and SNAT rule is removed. Immediate 502s stopped for majority of traffic. I'll keep monitoring and will update this thread with any regressions. :thumbsup:

devon_oncall: Post-action checklist created in the ticket with commands and expected outputs. Also recommending a scheduled DR test for DX failover to avoid asymmetric path issues.

maria_support: Closing for now but keeping incident open for follow-up and PM. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
